==Problem==
Two congruent circles centered at points <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> each pass through the other circle's center. The line containing both <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> is extended to intersect the circles at points <math>C</math> and <math>D</math>. The circles intersect at two points, one of which is <math>E</math>. What is the degree measure of <math>\angle CED</math>?

<math>\textbf{(A) }90\qquad\textbf{(B) }105\qquad\textbf{(C) }120\qquad\textbf{(D) }135\qquad \textbf{(E) }150</math>

==Solution==
===Solution 1===
Observe that <imath>\triangle{EAB}</imath> is equilateral (all are radii of congruent circles). Therefore, <imath>m\angle{AEB}=m\angle{EAB}=m\angle{EBA} = 60^{\circ}</imath>. Since <imath>CD</imath> is a straight line, we conclude that <imath>m\angle{EBD} = 180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=120^{\circ}</imath>. Since <imath>BE=BD</imath> (both are radii of the same circle), <imath>\triangle{BED}</imath> is isosceles, meaning that <imath>m\angle{BED}=m\angle{BDE}=30^{\circ}</imath>. Similarly, <imath>m\angle{AEC}=m\angle{ACE}=30^{\circ}</imath>. 

Now, <imath>\angle{CED}=m\angle{AEC}+m\angle{AEB}+m\angle{BED} = 30^{\circ}+60^{\circ}+30^{\circ} = 120^{\circ}</imath>. Therefore, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C) }\ 120}</imath>.
